title: Memoized Selectors
definition: Selectors that cache their previous inputs and outputs. If the state hasn't changed, they return the cached result instantly instead of recalculating the derived state.
simpleExplanation: If your selector sorts an array of 10,000 users alphabetically, that takes processing power. If the user clicks a button that changes the 'Dark Mode' theme, the component re-renders and the selector runs again, sorting the 10,000 users again for no reason. A memoized selector remembers the sorted list, and says 'The users didn't change, here is the cached list instantly.'
realWorldExample: Using the `createSelector` utility from the `Reselect` library (which is built into RTK) to prevent expensive map/filter/reduce operations from freezing the UI.

basic: What RTK function is used to create a memoized selector?
intermediate: If a memoized selector returns a new array using `.map()`, will it cause unnecessary re-renders?

answers.question: Unnecessary re-renders?
answers.answer: Without memoization, yes. `.map()` creates a brand new array reference every time it runs, causing React to think the data changed. Memoization fixes this by returning the EXACT SAME array reference from the cache.
